classification.difficultyReason: Find the intersection of two lines by elimination, then verify that it lies on the third line.

content.prompt: Show that the straight lines $2x-3y=7$, $3x-4y=13$ and $8x-11y=33$ meet at a point.

answer.short:
All three lines meet at $(11,5)$.

Eliminate one variable using the first two equations, then check their intersection in the third equation.
answer.worked:
Multiply the first equation by $3$ and the second by $2$:

$$\begin{align*}6x-9y&=21\\6x-8y&=26\end{align*}$$

Subtracting gives:

$$\begin{align*}(6x-8y)-(6x-9y)&=26-21\\y&=5\end{align*}$$

Substitute $y=5$ into $2x-3y=7$:

$$\begin{align*}2x-3(5)&=7\\2x&=22\\x&=11\end{align*}$$

Check the third line:

$$\begin{align*}8(11)-11(5)&=88-55\\8(11)-11(5)&=33\end{align*}$$

Thus $(11,5)$ satisfies all three equations, so the three lines meet at this point.
